text:
Brandon Hagel had two goals and an assist in Columbus on Thursday, his third straight game with a goal, and Tampa has now won five of six. He has 13 goals and 24 points in 19 games, nearly all of it at even strength: only four of his points have come on the power play.

He's earning it. His 13 goals came on 12.4 expected, so the finishing is honest. If anything, Hagel has been unlucky. Tampa owns almost 65% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice, and its share is 13 points better than when he sits, but the team has scored 6.7 fewer goals than those chances deserve. That usually swings back toward more points.

Evolving-Hockey had him in the 99th percentile among forwards for creating expected goals last season, with teammates and opponents accounted for, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him near the top in both setting up chances and getting to the slot. For a sixth-round pick, that's a complete player. His ice time dipped a little over his last ten games. Watch whether it comes back as the goals keep coming.
headline: Hagel's line is winning more than it's scoring
